suppliers.subject: 30 ml cylindrical frosted-glass serum bottle + dropper closure — technical specification and decoration request
suppliers.body:
Hello,

We are specifying packaging for a 30 ml cylindrical frosted-glass cosmetic serum bottle with a metallic collar and dropper closure. We need manufacturer specification data rather than marketing copy, for one exact product variant that you can actually supply.

CONTAINER — please send:
  - exact supplier and product code
  - bottle technical drawing (CAD or dimensioned PDF)
  - nominal capacity and overflow capacity
  - body diameter, overall height, shoulder height
  - neck finish, neck outer diameter, neck inner diameter
  - glass weight and any wall or construction notes
  - dimensional tolerances
  - frosting/coating capability and colour capability
  - print-zone drawing and flat artwork dimensions
  - recommended decoration process

CLOSURE — please send:
  - exact supplier and closure product code
  - compatible neck finish
  - collar outer diameter and collar height
  - bulb dimensions, pipette dimensions, dip-tube length
  - closure technical drawing and material specification
  - finish and colour options
  - torque or assembly guidance
  - dimensional tolerances

COMPATIBILITY — please confirm in writing:
  - that the quoted bottle and closure are a compatible pair
  - assembled sample photographs
  - leakage-test information, and drop/transport-test data if held
  - recommended filling-line or assembly requirements

MATERIALS — please state the available options and tolerances for:
  - body: glass type, frosting method, colour/spraying system, durability, adhesion, chemical resistance, colour tolerance
  - collar: aluminium grade, anodizing or coating process, gloss level, surface treatment, corrosion resistance
  - closure: elastomer compound, hardness, colour options, compatibility with a cosmetic oil formula, chemical-resistance and migration data

DECORATION — please state which of screen printing, pad printing, hot stamping, foil, decal or UV printing you support on this item, together with maximum printable width and height, safe margin, wrap angle, any artwork distortion compensation you apply, colour count, registration tolerance, minimum line width, minimum readable text size, and your artwork file requirements.

COLOUR — for each decoration process you offer on this item, please state which colour systems you accept artwork in (Pantone, CMYK or spot colours), what you can hold to in each, and any colour tolerance you state.

Finally, please confirm MOQ, sample availability and lead time.

A dimensional drawing or CAD file is the single most useful item — our current geometry is a design concept and we will not treat it as production authority until your drawing confirms it.

Thank you.

receipts.finding: The submitted file hashes exactly to the frozen accepted source, so it is byte-identical to the original and cannot be the product of an open/save/reopen cycle in Illustrator. A verification copy necessarily differs from the source it was saved from.

receipts.subject: docs/visual_quality/vq2/vq2_a2_r2_final.ai
receipts.observed: the complete product opened as one solid black silhouette
receipts.gate_a_effect: NONE — Gate A remains BLOCKED; the source is superseded by a corrected one that is itself not yet verified
receipts.finding: This is a real Illustrator execution result, and it FAILED. The cause is a source colour-emission defect, not an Illustrator display preference: every visible object in the accepted .ai was written as 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 Xa and the document declared Black only, while the accepted PDF and PNG proofs committed alongside it carried the four correct colours. The source and the proofs were therefore not equivalent in colour. A corrected source has been generated from the same geometry and awaits a new human round trip; it is NOT itself verified, and Gate A has not moved.

receipts.subject: docs/visual_quality/vq2/vq2_a2_r2_final_gate_a_r1.ai
receipts.observed: body, collar and closure rendered in their approved colours; logo, registered symbol, divider, Rose, Damascena and NIGHT REPAIR OIL all absent from the visible result
receipts.finding: The R1 colour repair worked - the three visible objects carry their approved colours, which R0 did not. A different defect remains: 37 of 40 objects do not reach the visible result. Measured in the repo, all 37 missing objects lie fully inside the body's bounding box and the 3 survivors are exactly those the body does not cover. That fits two explanations equally well - the body stacking above the artwork, or Illustrator discarding content after the third layer block - and this environment cannot separate them, so neither is recorded as the cause. R2 removes layer blocks and inherited state entirely, so it does not depend on which is true.

receipts.subject: docs/visual_quality/vq2/vq2_a2_r2_final_gate_a_r2.ai
receipts.observed: body, collar, closure, BBROSE logo, medallion and registered symbol, divider, Rose, Damascena and NIGHT REPAIR OIL all visible in approved colours, as separate Path and Compound Path objects
receipts.finding: This is the first Illustrator run of this artwork that lost nothing, and it closes the second defect: R1 rendered 3 of 40 objects, R2 renders all of them. Illustrator also built real vector objects rather than embedding the EPS - the owner reports separate Path and Compound Path items, so the compound paths carrying the counters and the medallion survived as objects. What it does NOT establish is Gate A. The returned .ai hashes exactly to the R2 source, so it is the original re-uploaded and nothing was saved, closed or reopened; a verification copy necessarily differs from the file it was saved from. Any uploaded PDF/PNG that matches this repository's own R2 proofs is likewise a re-upload and carries no Illustrator provenance. Neither upload reached this environment, so neither was hashed here.
receipts.does_not_isolate_r1_mechanism: R2 changed several things at once, so this does not say whether R1 lost its artwork to stacking or to a dropped layer boundary. Fixture A would still separate them; that is now forensic, not blocking.

receipts.subject: vq2_a2_r2_final_illustrator_verified.ai (as submitted)
receipts.finding: The first genuinely different file to come back, and a native Illustrator document rather than our EPS - a save really happened. Measured here from the file itself: 40 vector objects, 39 filled plus the divider stroke, all four approved colours and nothing else, zero rasters, zero live text. The artwork passed. The page did not: 763.654 x 983.225 pt against the accepted 207.1627 x 493.2283. The ink measures the same physical height as the source, so the artwork was translated, never resized. This is a defect in the automation script, not in the artwork.
receipts.second_finding: The result JSON on disk came from a DIFFERENT, aborted run in which the .jsx was selected instead of the .ai; it records FAIL with save, reopen and both exports false, and it overwrote the record belonging to the run that produced this copy. The copy is still genuine, but its script-written provenance was destroyed. Both script defects are now fixed.

receipts.subject: vq2_a2_r2_final_illustrator_verified.ai
receipts.finding: The round trip completed and every figure was re-measured here from the returned files rather than taken from the report: all four hashes match, the artboard is 207.162994 x 493.227997 pt, there are 40 logical drawings, 39 filled plus the divider stroke, only the four approved colours, no raster and no live text. The submitted JSON records human_result PASS with save, reopen and both exports true, no warning, and both nine-item human confirmations answered. Gate A passes.

supplier_sent_validation.why_a_claim_is_not_evidence: the eight checks are about a message that exists — its destination, its subject, its body hash, its Date and its Message-ID. None of those can be read from a statement that sending happened. Neither a statement nor a verified message moves the count: only the owner's typed sent date does.
